title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources
summary: Hold: Microsoft now explicitly says existing connector allow/block controls apply through Work IQ APIs, contrary to the briefing's repeated caveats. Work IQ API billing is documented as usage-based Copilot Credits consumption, so presenting that billing as unconfirmed background and rating cost solely from connector add-on licences would mislead administrators.

claims.where: What's changing: How Work IQ will surface them
claims.claim: How Work IQ surfaces federated connectors is not described in detail.
claims.quote:
Connected enterprise sources participate in Work IQ Copilot, entity, and schema tools. Connected enterprise sources refer to data sources connected in Copilot Chat.

Connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Learn now describes connected enterprise sources as participating in Work IQ Copilot, entity and schema tools; connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs. The roadmap still lists this item as In development.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated Copilot connectors fetch external data in real time using MCP.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors access data using the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: existing settings
claims.claim: Administrators manage federated connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The source system enforces permissions for federated connector access.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not copy source data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use OAuth 2.0.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.
claims.fix: Remove 'Uses OAuth 2.0 and' and retain 'Uses the user's permissions in the source system.' The cited overview supports OAuth, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/set-up-custom-federated-connectors also lists 'No Auth' with 'Users don't need to authenticate.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector supplies tools, Copilot can create, update or delete source data.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.

claims.claim: Connector write tools require user approval.
claims.quote: Tools that create, update, or delete data initially require the user's explicit approval. Users can choose whether Copilot asks again for that tool, as described in Confirm an action.

claims.claim: New write tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: Federated connectors remain read-only in Researcher.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: The general Copilot connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only.
claims.quote: Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: MCP servers restricting incoming traffic by source IP may need static egress IP allow-listing.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Existing federated Copilot connectors require a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7 for querying users.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.claim: The Work IQ capability's licensing model is add-on.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'consumption'. Replace the notes with 'Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and uses usage-based billing through Copilot Credits. Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools have separate connector-specific licensing requirements.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/ and retain the Foundry prerequisites source for the separate connection paths.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Published Work IQ API billing and connector-licensing guidance are not confirmed rules for this capability.
claims.quote: Work IQ API through A2A, REST, or MCP | Usage-based billing | Enable billing with Copilot Credits. This path doesn't use connector licensing.
claims.fix: Remove 'Microsoft has not published whether this Work IQ capability changes those requirements' and 'Neither is a confirmed rule for this roadmap capability.' Replace 'Background, labelled separately:' with 'For Work IQ API access:'. Add 'The Foundry prerequisites distinguish Work IQ API access through A2A, REST or MCP, which uses Copilot Credits and does not use connector licensing, from connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools, whose connector-specific requirements must be checked.' Keep the existing connector add-on requirement explicitly scoped to those connectors, not Work IQ API access.

claims.claim: The Work IQ API uses a usage-based model paid through Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The preview Foundry Work IQ page says a connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for each calling user.
claims.quote: Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools | Connector licensing | Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites. A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.

claims.claim: Cost is medium because the documented cost is a connector add-on rather than applicable metered Work IQ consumption.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage and can be managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits; connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools have separate connector-specific licence requirements.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/ in the licensing section.
